title: Check Brackets Outside Quotes
description: Return whether `()`, `[]`, and `{}` are correctly balanced. Ignore bracket characters inside single- or double-quoted strings. Backslash escapes the next character inside a quoted string. Other characters are allowed.

solution.explanation: Track open brackets with a stack, while quote and escape state tells the scanner when bracket characters are part of string text. Each closing bracket must match the newest unmatched opener. The final stack and quote state must both be empty.

wrongSolutions:
def brackets_balanced(text):
    return text.count("(")==text.count(")") and text.count("[")==text.count("]") and text.count("{")==text.count("}")

tests.hint: No brackets or quotes are balanced.
A matching pair closes the most recent opener.
Closing brackets must match the latest opener.
Every opening bracket needs a close.
A close with no opener is invalid.
Brackets inside a quoted string are ignored.
This closing bracket has no matching opening bracket.
An unclosed quote makes the input invalid.
An escaped quote does not end the string.
Brackets in structured text balance normally.
A long surrounding text should not affect a balanced pair.
